answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers. Draw 8 Zoo cards and keep 4 (discard the other 4). Draw 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I; Animals goes in the leftmost slot (strength 1), and the other four are randomly assigned to the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for the second, 2 for the third, and 3 for the fourth.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C3: 1 active worker and remaining 3 lying down; D: 25 money; E: draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: draw 8, keep 4, discard 4; B: side I, Animals under leftmost slot and remaining four randomly; C1: appeal staggered 0/1/2/3.

answers.answer: Setup places 4 face-up Base Conservation Projects below the Association board in a 4-player game and 3 in games with fewer players. In a 2-player game, cover one level on each of the three face-up projects (left level of left card, middle of middle card, right of right card) and cover the three spaces in the donation area's left column; both players are blocked from those spaces. In 3- and 4-player games no such blocking is described. Reveal the initial 6-card display after all players have chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c specifies 4 projects for 4 players, otherwise 3, and the listed 2-player blocks; setup G says reveal the display after hand-card choices.

answers.answer: After using a card in slot 4, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. Set the action's strength before performing it. Each X-token spent adds +1 strength and returns to the supply; X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action, and no player may hold more than 5. Resolve an effect labeled ‘after finishing’ only after completing the action and moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove used card, shift all cards left of the empty slot right, place used card in slot 1; X-tokens set strength before action, +1 each, max 5; ‘After finishing’ effects occur after the action including card movement.

answers.answer: You may not take a regular action that does nothing; use the alternative X-token action instead. Select an Action card, take exactly 1 X-token, move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right; slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. You cannot take this action if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says you may not do nothing; X-TOKEN action grants exactly 1 token and moves the selected card to slot 1; impossible at 5 tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches its last space, ignore any extra movement and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. The break occurs after that player's current turn is finished. Play then continues clockwise with the next player after the break.
answers.evidence: Break track: break after the end of the current turn, reaching the last space gives 1 X-token, and additional steps are ignored; break procedure says play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: Both Cards sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. On side I, choose either deck draws by the strength table (up to 3 cards, with a discard when required) or snap exactly 1 display card of any reputation at strength 5 or more; snapping has no deck draw. On side II, draw from the deck and/or from within reputation range in any order using the upgraded table; at strength 5 the table is 4 cards, discard 1. Alternatively snap exactly 1 display card at strength 3 or more, regardless of reputation, without a deck draw. The reputation restriction applies to the side-II draw option, not snapping. Display cards are replenished after the whole turn. Hand limit is checked at breaks only (3 cards, or 5 with the particular university).
answers.evidence: Cards action: side I advances 2 and offers draw or snap at 5+; side II advances 2 and offers deck/within-range draws or snap from 3; snapping is exactly one card regardless of reputation. Display refill waits until turn end; hand limit only at breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. At reputation 15, additional reputation stays at 15 and gives 1 appeal per excess reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: ‘Within reputation range’ is the matching folder plus lower-numbered folders; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further reputation yields 1 appeal per step; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than the action strength. Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but no two identical buildings in that action. Pay 2 money per space before placing each building. Your first building must touch at least one map border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces, not beyond the map, overlapping buildings, or on water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately gives 1 appeal, once.
answers.evidence: Build action specifies exact-one/size limit and side-II different buildings/total size; placement rules give first-border and later-adjacent requirements, water/rock and restricted-space limits, cost, kiosk spacing, and pavilion appeal.

answers.answer: Build I offers kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and the Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally offers the Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary (each size 5). The component list has 4 Petting Zoos, 4 Reptile Houses, and 4 Large Bird Aviaries; each zoo may have at most one of each special enclosure; other buildings can be repeated subject to the side-II no-identical-buildings-in-one-action limit. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Build I list and Build II additions/maxima appear in BUILD action; unique buildings only enter through Sponsor cards; full coverage except water/rock grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes: benefits gained earlier in an action—including money, cards, and newly activated workers—may be used in later steps of that action. Resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Thus, for example, earlier building placement bonuses can fund a later building, and an earlier Association task can provide a worker/bonus for a later task; the summary also requires an animal's full cost before its play-generated money pays out. Immediate effects resolve when earned; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action is complete (and the Action cards have moved). If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens/shared action rule says earlier action benefits may be used for later steps and each item must be paid before its own benefits; Build II takes placement bonuses before the next building; Association II uses earlier task bonuses later; simultaneous effects are in the owning player's chosen order.

answers.answer: For each animal, meet all its printed conditions, pay its cost, house it, then place its card and resolve effects. A partner zoo matching a continent on the card reduces cost by 3 money per matching continent icon (so a double icon reduces it by 6). An animal other than a Petting Zoo animal may occupy its own empty standard enclosure of at least the printed size; Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use their shown special enclosure, marking the required spaces with player tokens; there must be enough free capacity. Any printed water/rock adjacency requirement applies to the chosen enclosure and counts distinct adjacent terrain hexes. Immediate effects happen before the next animal; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the entire Animals action is done. If effects are simultaneous, the player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action lists conditions, payment and the 3-money reduction per continent icon, empty standard enclosure size, Petting Zoo-only animals, special-enclosure tokens/capacity, distinct water/rock adjacency, and immediate versus after-finishing timing.

answers.answer: Animals II allows animals from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; a display animal costs its folder number in addition to its normal cost. With strength 5 or more, first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the higher range applies to that action. The display is not replenished until the turn ends. Animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon may be played.
answers.evidence: Animals side II: display animals within reputation range with folder-number extra cost; at strength 5+ reputation increases by 1 at the action's very beginning; display refill waits until turn end; upgrade-required conditions are allowed.

answers.answer: Existing animals may be moved only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, once per building; they must be animals suitable for that special enclosure (reptiles and the birds that can use an aviary). Mark the spaces each animal occupies using player tokens; the summary gives no separate fixed number of animals that may move, so the available special-enclosure spaces limit how many fit. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain; if none, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip no standard enclosure. The summary does not specify a fixed numerical animal limit beyond available capacity.
answers.evidence: Build II allows immediate movement of suitable animals when either special enclosure is built. Special enclosures use tokens for the spaces shown on each animal, and insufficient free spaces prevent housing it. The movement rule gives the standard-enclosure selection and fallback.

answers.answer: The four Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. Side I performs exactly one task. Side II performs one or more different tasks whose total value is at most the action strength. Each chosen task needs 1 active worker, or 2 if one of yours is already on that task; if 3 of your workers are on it, you cannot do it again before the break. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association action lists the four strengths, side-I exactly-one rule, repeat-task worker requirement and other-player rule, and side-II different tasks with total value no greater than strength.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from the available spaces on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty matching column space on your map; take any printed space bonus immediately, and also advance reputation if shown on a university. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents. A player may have at most 4 partner zoos, and the third and fourth require upgraded Association. The third partner also requires Association II per the map/setup summary. Universities are the only way to raise the hand limit to 5; otherwise it is 3, checked only at breaks. The Association board replenishes partner zoos and universities at breaks so each is available exactly once, skipping ones all players already have. A bonus granting one must take an available Association-board tile, not one from general supply.
answers.evidence: Association tasks specify board source/map destination, immediate bonuses, different continents/max four/upgraded requirement, no duplicate universities and their hand-limit role; break procedure replenishes board tiles; FAQ clarifies tiles come from the board.

answers.answer: With Association I, conservation work can support a project already in play or play a project from hand and support it immediately. Association II can also play a new project from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number. A new project goes on the leftmost space above the Association board and shifts existing projects right; the allowed number above the board is 2, 3, or 4 according to player count. To support a project, fulfill a condition with no token and place one of your player tokens from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition; each project may be supported only once by you. Taking the token activates its map bonus immediately, and you choose whether to take that bonus before or after the project reward. If a new project exceeds the row limit, discard the rightmost project and return tokens on it to their owners' supplies; already activated map bonuses remain activated. Base projects below the board never move.
answers.evidence: Association project-work rules specify hand/display entry, support condition and one-time limit, token source, bonus timing, row limits and overflow-token destination; base projects below never move.

answers.answer: Yes. A released animal must require a standard enclosure of exactly the size shown by the release project, neither smaller nor larger, even if it could live in a special enclosure. First lose only its printed appeal; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. If it could live in a special enclosure, remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, including terrain; failing that, the smallest occupied one meeting its size requirement; if none meets even size, flip none. Playing a new release project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
answers.evidence: Release project rules specify exact standard-size match; loss/retention; special tokens first and standard-enclosure fallback; new versus existing release-project reputation.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if action strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Alternatively, advance the Break token by the action strength and take that much money even if fewer steps are needed to reach the last space. Sponsors II plays one or more cards if strength +1 is at least their combined levels; X-tokens can raise strength above 5. Cards may come from hand or from the display within reputation range, with the folder number paid as extra cost. Resolve cards one by one, fully resolving each card's instant effects except ‘after finishing’ effects before the next; display cards are not replenished until turn end. The side-II break option pays twice the amount. The summary explicitly says full money is paid on side I even when only one break step remains; it does not separately restate that edge case for side II, though side II doubles the money option.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action gives side-I/II level rules, display use/cost and sequential resolution; side I takes full money even if the token does not need all steps, and side II's break option pays twice.

answers.answer: Break order: (1) discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the particular university); (2) return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens from Action cards; (3) recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; (4) discard display folders 1–2, move remaining cards down and refill; (5) take income: appeal-track money, kiosk income, then Sponsor-card and activated map break income; (6) reset the Break token. Each kiosk earns 1 per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, while empty special enclosures do. Adjacency means sharing at least one side. When multiple players take display cards during income, refill after each player; usually income is simultaneous, but if order is needed start with the break initiator (or affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Break procedure enumerates all six steps and kiosk income neighbors; the income-order note specifies refill after each player and clockwise ordering when effects require it.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus token next to that space (a taken token is removed; the 5-money choice remains if tokens are gone). At 10, the first player to reach or exceed it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10, all discard one before scoring. Check the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when appeal and conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits for the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end unless someone else triggers it first. A triggering player finishes their turn; then every other player gets one final turn. If triggered during a break, every player gets one final turn. Each Final Scoring card can give at most 4 conservation points. VP equals your Appeal value minus the lowest Appeal value in your Conservation counter's scoring area. Highest positive VP wins; ties go to the player with the most supported projects (tokens removed from the map), then tied players share the victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions specify rewards at 2, 5, 8, 10; end check timing and delayed appeal; final turns; 4-point card cap; VP formula and tiebreak.
